title: R E A C T : S YNERGIZING R EASONING AND ACTING IN LANGUAGE MODELS
abstract: This paper introduces ReAct, a novel paradigm that combines reasoning and acting in language models for solving diverse language reasoning and decision making tasks. ReAct prompts large language models to generate both verbal reasoning traces and actions pertaining to a task in an interleaved manner.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're cooking a dish in the kitchen. Between any two specific actions, you may reason in language to track progress, handle exceptions, or realize when external information is needed. This tight synergy between "acting" and "reasoning" allows humans to learn new tasks quickly and perform robust decision making or reasoning.

ReAct brings this synergy to large language models, enabling them to generate both reasoning traces and task-specific actions in an interleaved manner.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content: ReAct augments the agent's action space to include language, allowing the model to generate thoughts or reasoning traces that update the context and support future reasoning or acting. The model can interact with external environments, such as a Wikipedia API, to incorporate additional information into reasoning.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content: ReAct outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on HotpotQA and Fever, with an absolute improvement of 5.8% and 4.5% respectively. On ALFWorld and WebShop, ReAct achieves an absolute improvement of 34% and 10% in success rates respectively.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content: ReAct's combination of reasoning and acting enables more interpretable and trustworthy decision making. By generating reasoning traces, ReAct provides a clear understanding of the model's thought process, allowing for easier identification of errors or biases.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content: ReAct's key innovations include its ability to generate both verbal reasoning traces and task-specific actions in an interleaved manner, and its use of external knowledge bases to inform reasoning. This enables ReAct to outperform state-of-the-art baselines on a range of tasks.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content: To try ReAct yourself, you can use the provided code and experiment with different tasks and environments. You can also explore the potential applications of ReAct in areas such as question answering, fact verification, and decision making.
